Co-doped ZnO powders were synthesized via Sol-Gel method with Co doping levels of 0%, 3%, 6%, 9%, and 12%.
The powders exhibited hexagonal wurtzite crystal structure confirmed by XRD with no secondary phases.
SEM analysis showed spherical particles with an average size of approximately 120 nm.
EDX spectra confirmed the presence of Zn, O, and Co elements, verifying successful Co doping.
Room temperature ferromagnetism was observed in all samples, including undoped ZnO due to oxygen vacancies.
Saturation magnetization increased from 0.035 emu/g (undoped) to 0.12 emu/g at 12% Co doping.
Coercivity was measured as 3.4 × 10^4 A/m for the doped powders.
Co-doped ZnO powders were embedded in styrofoam sheets at varying loading levels to form composites.
Radar absorption was measured in the X-band frequency range (8–12 GHz) using a network analyzer.
The composite with 12% Co-doped ZnO showed a maximum radar absorption of 93% at 10.9 GHz.
Increasing the Co doping concentration and powder loading level both enhanced radar absorption performance.
The radar absorption peak for 9% Co-doped ZnO at 4x loading reached 93.5% at 8.46 GHz.
The substitutional doping of Co ions into Zn sites did not distort the ZnO crystal lattice.
Oxygen vacancies created during calcination contribute to ferromagnetism in ZnO powders.
Magnetic properties and radar absorption are correlated; higher magnetization corresponds to higher absorption.
The powders were sintered at 500°C for 3 hours to remove impurities.
The study used zinc acetate dihydrate and cobalt(II) acetate as precursors.
The wet gel was treated at 130°C for 12 hours before sintering.
Radar-absorbing materials help reduce radar cross-section by absorbing and minimizing reflected radar waves.
Co-doped ZnO reinforced styrofoam composites are lightweight and have potential for stealth technology applications.
